summary: The proposal has a coherent focus and appears to provide a concrete platform and evaluation plan, but it needs revision before submission. The main issues are that the Problem section includes workaround solutions and that first-person phrasing is used extensively; additional editing should clarify actors and standardize terminology.

findings.title: Problem section presents workaround solutions
findings.description: Remove or reframe the workaround examples in the Problem section so it focuses on the underlying problems and their negative consequences. The resulting risks, such as obscured accountability and excessive privileges, can remain.

locations.quote: A student who needs a host, a channel, and a repository asks several people and waits for each of them, and some bridge the delay with **a shared login that hides who acted**.

**The common workaround hands maintainers full administrative rights**, which violates the principle of least privilege [SS75] and exposes every user and every host to a mistake made for a single project.

findings.title: Repeated first-person phrasing
findings.description: Replace repeated first-person singular constructions with the thesis, platform, or study as the grammatical subject, in accordance with the guideline to avoid “I.” Retain first person only where the transparency statement requires explicit authorship.

locations.quote: In this thesis, **I develop** a self-service platform on which every grant carries an expiry date from the moment somebody requests it.
In this thesis, **I develop** a self-service platform on which requesters ask for time-limited access, maintainers decide, and access ends on its own.

locations.section: 4.1 Unify Heterogeneous Resources in One Tree
locations.quote: **I implement** the keycloak-group, slack-channel, github-team, and webhook connectors.

locations.section: 4.2 Enforce an Expiry Date on Every Grant
locations.quote: **I evaluate** correctness with an automated scenario that provisions SSH, Slack, and GitHub access from one approval.

locations.section: 4.3 Delegate the Approval of Requests to Maintainers
locations.quote: **I reach** this objective when administrators perform fewer manual actions and requesters wait less than in the current process.
Iteration 1, 1–28 October (Objective 1): **I deliver** the Keycloak realm with OpenID Connect login, SSH key self-service, and the resource tree with inherited maintainers.

findings.title: Passive constructions obscure actors
findings.description: Rewrite passive or reduced passive constructions with explicit subjects and active verbs so that the responsible actor is clear. For example, use “the project grants access that outlives...” and “after I write the connector...” or “after disabling the workflow engine...” where appropriate.

locations.quote: Requests travel by chat message or e-mail, nobody records an end date, and **access granted for one project** outlives the time a person spends at the chair.

locations.section: 4.1 Unify Heterogeneous Resources in One Tree
locations.quote: I reach this objective when the webhook connector, **written after I freeze the framework**, needs one new class and one registry entry.

locations.section: 4.2 Enforce an Expiry Date on Every Grant
locations.quote: I evaluate correctness with an automated scenario that provisions SSH, Slack, and GitHub access from one approval, and, in a second run with the **workfow engine disabled on purpose**, the drift check reports the remaining SSH membership.

findings.title: Inconsistent spelling of “e-mail”
findings.description: Choose one spelling for the term and apply it consistently throughout the proposal’s prose. The cited passages use the hyphenated form “e-mail”; verify that the preferred form is used consistently elsewhere as well.

locations.quote: Requests travel by chat message or **e-mail**, nobody records an end date, and access granted for one project outlives the time a person spends at the chair.
I deliver recertifcation campaigns with escalation, the drift report, and **e-mail** notifications.
